<!-- pr-reviewer: 873c76b4d34b7bc45b118ca207332a58f42e9e1b -->
**Needs changes before merge.** This review covers the #801 commit `873c76b4` on top of #791's `40f256b4`, as the stack asks. The reverse crossing, the slit refusal and the inch and G41/G42 pins all hold up under probing. One gap remains in the slug tip-up. The departure exemption also covers a rapid that starts ON the hole's ring, and that hides a real crossing of the hole's own slug. The generator produces this case for every small hole and for any hole cut with lead-out 0.

### What looks good
- **The reverse crossing (`sim/src/verify/plasma/mod.rs:221`).** I ran the third #791 review's nesting probes in all six orders of part P (in the hole), hole H and outline O. I ran each order twice: once with P clear of the hole's wall and once with P touching it.
  - **Clear:** P,H,O gives `[]`. PH,P,H,O (the nested part's own hole first) also gives `[]`. Every other order is refused by `CutOrder`.
  - **Touching:** P,H,O gives only `KerfCrossing`, which is legal common-line cutting. Each order that cuts P after H is refused (`CutCrossing` and/or `CutOrder`).
  - **Two OUTER parts sharing an edge:** I tried a full shared edge, a partial shared edge (offset 10 mm), a shorter rectangle against the edge and a corner touch. In both orders, each case gives only `KerfCrossing`. Parts-in-holes and common lines stay legal.
  - **Other cases are refused:** an earlier hole of one part overlapped by a later part is a `CutCrossing`, and an earlier part lying wholly inside a later part's material is refused as `Malformed` (parent disagreement).
- **A different earlier slug is judged.** A rapid that leaves hole 3 (the hole just cut) and crosses earlier hole 2 is `TipUp { freed: 2, slug: true }`. The L-shaped "back over its own slug" pin holds.
- **The slit refusal (`motion/src/plasma/nest.rs:63`).**
  - **Legal shapes still generate:** many collinear vertices; near-duplicate points 1e-5 and 1e-7 apart; 0.5 µm and 2 µm bumps on an edge; a 3 x 1 mm notch; a 720-chord circular hole.
  - **Exact zero-width slits are refused** with the new message, wherever they are: a diagonal slit, an outward spike, a slit in a hole contour, and a slit 0.3 µm off-axis.
  - **Near-zero slits** of width 1e-5, 1e-4, 5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3, 0.01 and 0.1 mm all fall to the cover law's "narrower than the kerf" refusal. A 0.6 mm notch does too.
  - No input silently drops the slit.
- **Inch and G41/G42.** `describe` formats through `units::len` with the document's suffix, and the inch pin checks both the inch and the mm strings. The G41/G42 pin compares the control program's rings with the computer-offset program's rings point by point (1e-6).
- **Remove-the-refusal spot checks (two), source restored after each.**
  - Dropping the `.or_else(... rings_cross(theirs, mine) ...)` reverse check fails `plasma_laws::a_part_cut_around_an_earlier_ring_running_through_it_is_refused`.
  - Disabling `dropped_vertex` fails `plasma::tests::a_zero_width_slit_in_a_picked_contour_is_refused_not_dropped`.
- **Process.** The commit subject is conventional, the body has a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #801`, and there is a decision file. There is no `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot, golden, dependency, build-script, workflow or process-file change. The new non-test code has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`: `dropped_vertex` indexes `ring[k]` and `ring[(k + 1) % n]` only with `k < n`.

### Local results (head 873c76b4 trial-merged with upstream main e2d655e5: clean, no conflicts)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | built |
| sim `plasma_laws` | 21 passed |
| sim `plasma_program` | 6 passed |
| motion `plasma::tests` | 16 passed |
| app `plasma_gate` | 6 passed |
| app `plasma_profile` | 7 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| app `golden_cl` | 24 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **`crates/sim/src/verify/plasma/geom.rs:150`: a rapid that starts ON the hole's ring and runs straight across that hole's slug is never judged.** The line is `let skip = usize::from(departing && (inside(a, ring) || on_ring(a, ring)));`.
   - **Why it misses:** when `a` is on the ring, the first piece runs from `a` to the next contact. If the rapid heads outward, that piece is outside, so it is never flagged anyway. If it heads inward, the piece IS the crossing of the slug. So the `on_ring` half of the exemption never excuses a departure. It only hides crossings.
   - **Probes** (hole `square(40,40,20)`, cut just before; the same geometry as an OUTER part warns):
     ```
     rapid (40,50) -> (110,50)   from the hole's left wall straight across its slug   => []
     rapid (40,40) -> (110,110)  from its corner along the diagonal                    => []
     same first rapid, part square(140,40,20) Outer                                     => [TipUp { slug: false, at: (150, 50) }]
     ```
   - **The generator produces this case.** A small hole has no lead-out by the small-hole rule, so it ends on its ride after the overburn (`motion/src/plasma/emit.rs:150-152`). Any hole cut with `lead_out = 0` ends on the ring too. That makes the "a hole's lead-out ends inside its own slug" premise of decision 1 false for exactly the small holes the decision chose not to exempt ("considered and dropped: exempting the `small` holes").
   - **Fix:** exempt the first piece only when the rapid starts strictly inside the slug: `departing && inside(a, ring)`.
     - With that change, all 21 `plasma_laws` pass and both probes above warn.
     - Three `plasma_program` fixtures fail, because their hand-built hole cuts end on the ring and the next rapid crosses the slug: `the_spans_become_cuts_and_the_travel_between_them_the_rapids` at (45, 40.9); `lit_arcs_are_chorded_into_the_cut` (a small hole) at (48.2, 40.3); and `a_rapid_over_a_freed_hole_slug_is_read_and_warned`, which gains extra findings. These fixtures are instances of this case. They need either a rapid that leaves outward or an expected `TipUp`.
     - Please pin the on-ring probe in `plasma_laws`, and adjust the "inside or on the ring" sentence in `docs/decisions/801-plasma-followups.md`.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **The departure piece can span the whole slug.** A lead-out that ends near one wall, followed by a rapid out through the opposite wall, crosses most of the slug unjudged. This is the stated design (the torch is already over the slug), and it is reasonable. A future refinement could judge the departure piece against the slug when it is longer than the shortest way out. That is a possible follow-up, not a request here.
- **Warnings, not refusals, for slugs: agreed.** Whether a slug drops depends on slat pitch, which the program does not know. That matches the part tip-up law, and the decision records it.
- **`crates/motion/src/plasma/nest.rs:131-135`: misplaced doc comment.** `ON_RING` and `dropped_vertex` were inserted between `open_run`'s doc comment and `open_run`. Rustdoc now joins "An open run, deduplicated and checked..." onto `ON_RING`'s doc, and `open_run` loses its doc. Moving the two items above that comment fixes it.
- **The slit message assumes a slit.** "runs out to ... and back along the same line" also fires for any other picked vertex the region drops (e.g. a zero-area lobe). That is still a correct refusal, but the wording could be more general ("a picked vertex the closed contour no longer reaches").
- **Near-zero slits report "about 0.988 mm across".** The cover law's gap figure for a slit 1e-5 to 0.1 mm wide is the distance to the plate's top edge, not the slit's width. This is pre-existing (#791 review 3, note 6). The refusal is right; only the figure is wrong.
- **`crates/sim/tests/plasma_laws.rs` is 404 lines**, just over the ~400 guideline. Noted only. If the fix's pin lands there, it may be time to split the #801 cases into their own file.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 7755b10379d5ec337af99bcb4c082e2ee5ae0a8e -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a delta review of 873c76b4..7755b103 ("fix(sim): a rapid from a hole's wall over its slug is a tip-up"), which answers the needs-rework blocker from the previous review.

### What looks good
- `crates/sim/src/verify/plasma/geom.rs:153`: the departure skip is now `departing && inside(a, ring)`. A hole with no lead-out ends on its own wall, and a rapid from there is now judged in full. An outward first piece is never inside the ring, so exempting "on the ring" never excused anything real. It only hid crossings over the slug. The doc comment above it says the same thing.
- New pin `a_rapid_from_a_holes_wall_across_its_slug_is_a_tip_up` (`crates/sim/tests/plasma_laws.rs:411`) covers both cases. A rapid from an edge's middle across the slug and one from a corner across the slug each produce exactly one `TipUp { contour: 1, freed: 2, slug: true }`, placed inside the 40..60 slug. A rapid straight outward from the wall stays clear.
- **Spot-check:** I put `|| on_ring(a, ring)` back locally (never pushed). The new pin then fails at `plasma_laws.rs:419`, so it really guards the fix. I restored the code afterwards.
- Holes that do have a lead-out still get the departure skip, because their rapid starts strictly inside the slug. The first case of `a_rapid_over_a_freed_hole_slug_is_a_tip_up_naming_the_hole` pins this: left, middle, right, then the outline, with every rapid starting at a hole centre, is still clean. The L-hole pin (`a_rapid_leaving_a_hole_and_running_back_over_its_slug_is_a_tip_up`) still checks that a later piece back over the slug is caught.
- `plasma_program` fixtures:
  - The `OUTLINE` pierce moved to (50,-5). From the hole's end at (50,40), the rapid now runs straight down, outward. The old pierce at (-5,50) would have clipped the slug (x 40..50, y 40..~41.8). On the Ø20 circle in `lit_arcs_are_chorded_into_the_cut` it would have entered the circle, since the tangent at (50,40) is horizontal.
  - `the_spans_become_cuts_and_the_travel_between_them_the_rapids` still asserts the role, parent and point-for-point counts, the 5-point rings and the rapid pair (updated to the new pierce), and that the program is clean.
  - `lit_arcs_are_chorded_into_the_cut` keeps every chording assertion (more than 8 chord points, all on Ø20 within 0.02, the small mark) and is still clean.
  - `the_outline_cut_before_its_hole_is_refused_from_the_record` still expects exactly the CutOrder plus the TipUp. Nothing was weakened.
  - `a_rapid_over_a_freed_hole_slug_is_read_and_warned` now expects three tip-ups, and I checked each one by hand:
    - Rapid (70,40)->(30,50): it starts on the right hole's bottom wall and goes up-left. At x=60, y=42.5, so it crosses the right slug (contour 2, freed 1).
    - Rapid (30,40)->(105,50): it starts on the left hole's bottom wall and goes up-right. At x=40, y≈41.3, so it crosses the left slug (freed 2).
    - The same rapid then passes x 60..80 at y 44..46.7, over the right slug (freed 1).
  - The test also now asserts that all three are warnings, not refusals, and that each one's text names its own hole.
- `nest.rs`: the `open_run` doc comment is back above `open_run` instead of above `ON_RING`. The reworded slit message still contains `picked contour 1`, `X50.000 Y40.000` and `open run`, which `a_zero_width_slit_in_a_picked_contour_is_refused_not_dropped` asserts.
- `docs/decisions/801-plasma-followups.md` now reads "strictly inside", and the new paragraph states the ON-the-ring case and its pins. This matches the code.
- No process files, build.rs, `.github`, scripts, new dependencies, snapshot PNGs or `CHANGELOG.md` in the PR.

### Local results (merged with current main; the merge is clean)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build (sim, motion, app tests) | ok |
| sim `plasma_laws` | 22 passed |
| sim `plasma_program` | 6 passed |
| motion `--lib plasma::tests` | 16 passed |
| app `plasma_gate` | 6 passed |
| app `plasma_profile` | 7 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. Small holes (`emit.rs:138-158`) are lead-in from the centre with no lead-out, so they end on their wall. In a generated program, the rapid to the next pierce will now warn whenever that pierce lies on the slug side of the wall tangent. That is correct by the law as written: it is a warning, not a refusal, and the decision file deliberately drops a slat-spacing exemption. Expect more tip-up warnings on programs dense with small holes. A later follow-up could have the generator pick the small hole's start point facing the next pierce.
2. `crates/sim/tests/plasma_laws.rs` is now 426 lines, a little past the ~400 guide. It is a test file, so this is only noted.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
